APM span p99 latency by service
description:
p99 span duration per minute, grouped by OTel service.name. Drives every
"p99 latency" KPI in the tree. Source: spans forwarded to HEC by the
OTel collector's splunk_hec traces exporter.

The exporter currently lands events with sourcetype=httpevent (HEC
default) rather than the documented sourcetype=otel:traces, so we
accept both. Span duration is computed as end_time - start_time
(nanoseconds) when the legacy `duration_ns` field isn't present.
Span attributes are nested under `attributes.*` in the httpevent
payload; we lift `customer.tier` out for tier-aware filters.
base_search:
index=otel_traces sourcetype="otel:traces" service.name=*
| rename "service.name" as service_name
| rename "attributes.customer.tier" as customer_tier
| eval duration_ns = coalesce(duration_ns, end_time - start_time)
| bin _time span=1m
| stats perc99(duration_ns) as p99_ns by _time, service_name, customer_tier
| eval p99_ms = round(p99_ns / 1000000, 0)
identifying_name: apm span p99 latency by service

title: APM span error rate by service
description:
Per-minute error ratio (errors / total spans), grouped by service.name
and customer.tier so tier KPIs can specialise the same base search.
An "error" is any span whose OTel status.code is STATUS_CODE_ERROR
(set by the SDK on uncaught exceptions / 5xx responses) or whose
legacy `error` boolean was set on the resource attributes.
base_search:
index=otel_traces sourcetype="otel:traces" service.name=*
| rename "service.name" as service_name
| rename "attributes.customer.tier" as customer_tier
| rename "status.code" as status_code
| bin _time span=1m
| stats count(eval(status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR" OR 'error'="true")) as errors,
        count                                                          as total
        by _time, service_name, customer_tier
| eval error_rate = round(errors / total, 4)
identifying_name: apm span error rate by service

title: APM span request rate by service
description:
Per-minute SERVER-span count, divided by 60 to give RPS. Server
spans = inbound HTTP/grpc handlers, so this counts external calls
hitting each service. Filters on both the legacy `span_kind`
(otel:traces format) and the current `kind` field (httpevent
format) emitted by the splunk_hec exporter.
base_search:
index=otel_traces sourcetype="otel:traces"
  service.name=* (kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER" OR span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER")
| rename "service.name" as service_name
| rename "attributes.customer.tier" as customer_tier
| bin _time span=1m
| stats count as rpm by _time, service_name, customer_tier
| eval rps = round(rpm / 60.0, 2)
identifying_name: apm span request rate by service

title: RUM page load p95 (server-side proxy)
description:
Historical context (2026-06-11): the original implementation queried
`index=splunkrum event="page_view"` and assumed Log Observer Connect
was federating Splunk RUM page-view events from Splunk Observability
Cloud into a local `splunkrum` index on Splunk Enterprise. LOC was
never wired up in this demo, so the index doesn't exist and the KPI
sat at zero for every operator. The Customer Channel tile read "no
data" even during a live demo where the SPA was actually under load.

Current implementation: api-gateway server-side p95 latency for the
first XHR each SPA session makes (POST /process, which the user
triggers on Send Payment). This is a server-side proxy for the
user-perceived "the page is slow" signal:

  * When db-slow chaos hits, the gateway's call into ledger-service
    blocks, gateway p95 climbs, and the SPA's submit button visibly
    spins. The KPI moves.
  * When fraud-burst or latency-storm chaos hits, the gateway path
    stretches, p95 climbs, the SPA's "waiting" overlay extends. The
    KPI moves.
  * When kafka-outage hits, settlement returns 5xx and the gateway
    response time briefly spikes before failure mode kicks in. The
    KPI moves.

Caveats (presenter notes):
  * Does NOT capture the SPA's static-asset load (index.html, JS
    bundle, CSS) - that's served by nginx + the web-frontend pod,
    neither of which exports OTel spans for static GETs. The true
    first-contentful-paint signal only lives in Splunk Observability
    RUM (web vitals: rum.lcp.app.natwest-payments-web). To upgrade
    this KPI to the real RUM metric, configure the Splunk App for
    Splunk Observability Cloud (already installed at
    /opt/splunk/etc/apps/splunk_app_for_splunk_o11y_cloud) with a
    user-level API token (TF_VAR_splunk_api_token), then change the
    base search to:
      | rest /servicesNS/-/splunk_app_for_splunk_o11y_cloud/o11y-metrictimeseries
            program="data('rum.lcp.app.natwest-payments-web').percentile(95).publish()"
            start_time="-2m" end_time="now"
      | spath value | rename value AS p95_ms
  * The XHR p95 is a per-request signal, not a per-page-load signal.
    One slow XHR per page = one sample; the "page load p95" name is
    retained for ITSI/glass-table compatibility but the metric is
    better thought of as "first-XHR p95".

Splits the value by customer_tier so the Bronze / Silver / Gold
service tiles light up independently (matches the per-tier story
the synthetic-outcomes panel tells).
base_search:
index=otel_traces service.name=api-gateway name="POST /process"
| rename "attributes.customer.tier" as customer_tier
| eval duration_ms = (end_time - start_time) / 1000000
| eval customer_tier = coalesce(customer_tier, "unknown")
| bin _time span=1m
| stats perc95(duration_ms) as p95_ms by _time, customer_tier

title: Synthetic check success rate
description:
Historical context (2026-06-11): the original implementation queried
`index=splunkrum event="synthetic_run"` and assumed Splunk Synthetics
checks landed in a local `splunkrum` index via Log Observer Connect.
LOC was never wired up so the KPI read zero. The Customer Channel
tile showed "no data" even when our six ThousandEyes tests were
successfully probing the public SPA + API gateway URLs.

Current implementation: rolls up the http.server.request.availability
signal from ThousandEyes tests TE-01 (login page availability) and
TE-02 (API gateway availability), both of which already feed
index=thousandeyes via the Cisco ThousandEyes Add-on for Splunk's
Streaming integration (see scripts/09-configure-splunk-te-inputs.sh).

Why TE instead of Splunk Synthetics:
  * TE is already provisioned and configured for this demo
    (scripts/08-configure-thousandeyes.sh creates the six tests).
  * TE-01 + TE-02 directly probe the public demo URLs from five
    geographies, which is closer to a real customer's "is the bank
    up?" perspective than an internal Splunk Synthetic check would
    be.
  * Splunk Synthetics costs device-minutes; reusing TE costs
    nothing extra for this demo.

Failure semantics: success_rate = avg(http.server.request.availability) / 100,
where each TE probe returns 100 when its HTTP response matched the
configured status code AND content regex, else 0. We average across
both tests + all agents per minute so a single-agent flake doesn't
open a notable.

Caveat: TE-01 + TE-02 run every minute by default, which gives the
KPI ~5 samples per 5-minute window. If TE's streaming integration
stalls (we saw this for 40 days when the `enabled` flag on the
stream flipped to false in 2026-05), success_rate goes to N/A
rather than 0 because the bin produces no rows. The TE freshness
preflight check in scripts/00-preflight.sh catches that decay.
base_search:
index=thousandeyes sourcetype="cisco:thousandeyes:path-vis"
| rename "metric_name:http.server.request.availability" AS http_avail
| rename "thousandeyes.test.name" AS test_name
| where (test_name="LON NatWest Payments - SPA login page"
       OR test_name="LON NatWest Payments - API gateway recent"
       OR test_name="LON NatWest Payments - POST /api/process"
       OR test_name="LON NatWest Payments - SPA login page-load")
      AND isnotnull(http_avail)
| bin _time span=5m
| stats avg(http_avail) AS avg_avail by _time
| eval success_rate = round(avg_avail / 100, 3)

title: Kafka consumer lag growth (payments.settled, msg/min)
description:
Pulls Kafka consumer-group lag from settlement-service spans (the
OTel collector emits messaging.kafka.consumer.lag on consumer
`process` spans when kafkaConsumerEnabled=true). Reads both the
legacy top-level fields (messaging.system / messaging.operation /
messaging.kafka.consumer.lag) and their httpevent-flattened
attributes.* equivalents.
base_search:
| mstats latest(_value) AS plag WHERE index=itsi_im_metrics metric_name="kafka.consumer_group.lag" group="settlement-service" topic="payments.settled" span=1m BY partition
| stats sum(plag) AS total_lag BY _time
| sort 0 _time
| delta total_lag AS lag
| eval lag = if(isnull(lag) OR lag < 0, 0, lag)

title: EKS node host metrics
description:
EKS host CPU/memory utilization. itsi_im_metrics is a metric-type index
so the data is read with `| mstats` (event-style `index=… | stats` is a
no-op against a Splunk metric store - that's why every L4 metric KPI in
this file reads from mstats). Output column `v_pct` is host utilisation
0-100 %.
base_search:
| mstats avg(_value) AS v
    WHERE index=itsi_im_metrics
          metric_name IN ("system.cpu.utilization","system.memory.utilization")
    BY host.name, metric_name span=1m
| rename "host.name" AS host_name
| eval v_pct = round(v * 100, 1)

description:
Three Redis health signals stitched together from the OTel native
redis receiver and the redis_exporter prometheus scrape. Drives the
L4 nwpay_l4_redis service KPIs and feeds into the L3 microservices
that depend on it (sanctions-aml-service, fraud-detection-service).

itsi_im_metrics is a metric-type index, so the read path uses
`| mstats` (event-style `index=…` against a metric store returns
zero rows). The query pivots a single mstats aggregation over the
union of metric names by metric_name, so either the SignalFx-schema
native receiver names (redis.*) or the prometheus exporter names
(redis_*) populate the same output columns.
base_search:
| mstats max(_value) AS v
    WHERE index=itsi_im_metrics
          metric_name IN (
            "redis.keys.evicted",
            "redis.memory.used",
            "redis.clients.connected",
            "redis_evicted_keys_total",
            "redis_memory_used_bytes",
            "redis_connected_clients"
          )
    BY metric_name span=1m
| eval evicted_total     = case(metric_name IN ("redis.keys.evicted","redis_evicted_keys_total"), v),
       memory_used_bytes = case(metric_name IN ("redis.memory.used","redis_memory_used_bytes"), v),
       connected_clients = case(metric_name IN ("redis.clients.connected","redis_connected_clients"), v)
| stats max(evicted_total)     AS evicted_total,
        max(memory_used_bytes) AS memory_used_bytes,
        max(connected_clients) AS connected_clients
        BY _time
| streamstats current=t window=2 range(evicted_total) AS evictions_per_min
| eval evictions_per_min = coalesce(evictions_per_min, 0)

title: Postgres health (backends, cache, deadlocks, rollbacks, temp, commits, db_size, idle-in-tx)
description:
Eight Postgres health signals. Drives the L4 nwpay_l4_postgres KPIs
that ledger-service depends on. Cache hit ratio is computed from
pg_stat_database blocks_hit / blocks_read counters. commit/rollback
and temp_bytes counters are converted into per-period rates via
`streamstats range()` because the source is a monotonic counter.

itsi_im_metrics is a metric-type index; the read path uses
`| mstats`. Cumulative counters (commits, rollbacks, deadlocks,
temp_bytes) use `latest(_value)` per 1m bucket — `sum(_value)`
double-counts scrapes and breaks `streamstats range()`. Gauges
(backends, db_size, blocks_*) use the same latest aggregation.

pg_long_running_transactions has no `datname` dimension, so it is
fetched in a subsearch (without BY datname) and joined onto the
per-database rows as ledger-only signal.

Entity breakdown splits on the postgres_exporter `datname` dimension
(ledger + postgres). Instance-level gauges such as
pg_long_running_transactions are attributed to the application
database (ledger).
base_search:
| mstats latest(_value) AS v
    WHERE index=itsi_im_metrics
          metric_name IN (
            "pg_stat_database_numbackends",
            "pg_stat_database_deadlocks",
            "pg_stat_database_blks_hit",
            "pg_stat_database_blks_read",
            "pg_stat_database_xact_commit",
            "pg_stat_database_xact_rollback",
            "pg_stat_database_temp_bytes",
            "pg_database_size_bytes"
          )
    BY metric_name datname span=1m
| eval pg_database = if(isnotnull(datname) AND datname!="", datname, null())
| where isnotnull(pg_database) AND pg_database IN ("ledger","postgres")
| eval backends           = case(metric_name="pg_stat_database_numbackends",  v),
       deadlocks_total    = case(metric_name="pg_stat_database_deadlocks",   v),
       blocks_hit         = case(metric_name="pg_stat_database_blks_hit",     v),
       blocks_read        = case(metric_name="pg_stat_database_blks_read",    v),
       commits_total      = case(metric_name="pg_stat_database_xact_commit",   v),
       rollbacks_total    = case(metric_name="pg_stat_database_xact_rollback", v),
       temp_bytes_total   = case(metric_name="pg_stat_database_temp_bytes",   v),
       db_size_bytes      = case(metric_name="pg_database_size_bytes",         v)
| stats max(backends)          AS backends,
        max(deadlocks_total)   AS deadlocks_total,
        max(blocks_hit)        AS blocks_hit,
        max(blocks_read)       AS blocks_read,
        max(commits_total)     AS commits_total,
        max(rollbacks_total)   AS rollbacks_total,
        max(temp_bytes_total)  AS temp_bytes_total,
        max(db_size_bytes)     AS db_size_bytes
        BY _time, pg_database
| join type=left _time pg_database [
    | mstats latest(_value) AS long_running_txns
        WHERE index=itsi_im_metrics
              metric_name="pg_long_running_transactions"
        span=1m
    | eval pg_database="ledger"
  ]
| streamstats current=t window=2
        range(deadlocks_total)  AS deadlocks_per_min,
        range(commits_total)    AS commits_total_per_min,
        range(rollbacks_total)  AS rollbacks_per_min,
        range(temp_bytes_total) AS temp_bytes_per_min
        by pg_database
| eval deadlocks_per_min  = coalesce(deadlocks_per_min, 0),
       rollbacks_per_min  = coalesce(rollbacks_per_min, 0),
       temp_bytes_per_min = coalesce(temp_bytes_per_min, 0),
       commits_per_sec    = round(coalesce(commits_total_per_min, 0) / 60, 3),
       long_running_txns  = coalesce(long_running_txns, 0),
       cache_hit_ratio    = round(blocks_hit / (blocks_hit + blocks_read + 1), 4)
identifying_name: postgres health (backends, cache, deadlocks, rollbacks, temp, commits, db_size, idle-in-tx)

title: Kafka health (brokers, replication, latency, throughput, controller)
description:
Eight Kafka health signals. Drives the L4 nwpay_l4_kafka KPIs (in
addition to the existing consumer-lag KPI). Latency comes from the
JMX exporter's RequestMetrics MBean.

itsi_im_metrics is a metric-type index; the read path uses
`| mstats`. We compute avg+max+sum in a single mstats call and
pivot on metric_name so either the native kafkametrics receiver
names (kafka.*) or the JMX exporter names
(kafka_server_replicamanager_*, kafka_network_requestmetrics_*,
kafka_server_brokertopicmetrics_*, kafka_controller_*) populate
the same output columns.

Entity breakdown splits on the JMX scrape target
(`service.instance.id`, e.g. kafka.natwest.svc.cluster.local:5556).
The demo cluster runs a single combined controller+broker node.
base_search:
| mstats avg(_value) AS v_avg, max(_value) AS v_max, sum(_value) AS v_sum
    WHERE index=itsi_im_metrics
          metric_name IN (
            "kafka.brokers",
            "kafka.partition.under_replicated",
            "kafka_server_replicamanager_underreplicatedpartitions",
            "kafka_network_requestmetrics_totaltimems_99thpercentile",
            "kafka_server_brokertopicmetrics_messagesinpersec_oneminuterate",
            "kafka_server_brokertopicmetrics_bytesinpersec_oneminuterate",
            "kafka_controller_offlinepartitionscount",
            "kafka_controller_activecontrollercount",
            "kafka_server_replicamanager_isrshrinkspersec_count"
          )
    BY metric_name service.instance.id span=1m
| eval kafka_instance = coalesce(nullif(service.instance.id, ""),
                               "kafka.natwest.svc.cluster.local:5556")
| eval brokers_online           = case(metric_name="kafka.brokers", v_avg),
       under_replicated         = case(metric_name IN ("kafka.partition.under_replicated","kafka_server_replicamanager_underreplicatedpartitions"), v_max),
       request_p99_ms           = case(metric_name="kafka_network_requestmetrics_totaltimems_99thpercentile", v_max),
       messages_in_per_sec      = case(metric_name="kafka_server_brokertopicmetrics_messagesinpersec_oneminuterate", v_sum),
       bytes_in_per_sec         = case(metric_name="kafka_server_brokertopicmetrics_bytesinpersec_oneminuterate", v_sum),
       offline_partitions       = case(metric_name="kafka_controller_offlinepartitionscount", v_max),
       active_controller_count  = case(metric_name="kafka_controller_activecontrollercount", v_max),
       isr_shrinks_total        = case(metric_name="kafka_server_replicamanager_isrshrinkspersec_count", v_max)
| stats avg(brokers_online)          AS brokers_online,
        max(under_replicated)        AS under_replicated,
        max(request_p99_ms)          AS request_p99_ms,
        max(messages_in_per_sec)     AS messages_in_per_sec,
        max(bytes_in_per_sec)        AS bytes_in_per_sec,
        max(offline_partitions)      AS offline_partitions,
        max(active_controller_count) AS active_controller_count,
        max(isr_shrinks_total)       AS isr_shrinks_total
        BY _time, kafka_instance
| streamstats current=t window=2 range(isr_shrinks_total) AS isr_shrinks_per_min
        by kafka_instance
| eval brokers_online          = coalesce(brokers_online, 0),
       under_replicated        = coalesce(under_replicated, 0),
       request_p99_ms          = coalesce(request_p99_ms, 0),
       messages_in_per_sec     = coalesce(messages_in_per_sec, 0),
       bytes_in_per_sec        = coalesce(bytes_in_per_sec, 0),
       offline_partitions      = coalesce(offline_partitions, 0),
       active_controller_count = coalesce(active_controller_count, 0),
       isr_shrinks_per_min     = coalesce(isr_shrinks_per_min, 0)
identifying_name: kafka health (brokers, replication, latency, throughput, controller)

title: Banking audit - payment decline rate
description:
Decline ratio over the structured banking audit log. Distinct from
kbs_apm_error_rate: this counts business decisions (declined,
throttled, fraud, sanctions) rather than technical span errors, so
it stays clean during retries and partial failures. Drives the
"audited decline rate" KPI on L1 NatWest Card Payments and the
Authorization tier - the demo pivot from observability metric to
audited business event.
base_search:
index=nwpay_audit sourcetype="nwpay:payment_audit" event_type=payment_audit
| bin _time span=1m
| stats count(eval(decision IN ("rejected","throttled","error"))) as declined,
        count                                                      as total,
        count(eval(decision="rejected" AND decline_reason="sanctions_match"))  as sanctions_blocked,
        count(eval(decision="rejected" AND decline_reason="fraud_score_high")) as fraud_blocked
        by _time
| eval decline_rate    = round(declined / total, 4),
       sanctions_rate  = round(sanctions_blocked / total, 4),
       fraud_rate      = round(fraud_blocked / total, 4)

title: SPA authentication failure rate
description:
Authentication failure ratio per minute over the SPA auth beacon
stream. A spike here without a corresponding HTTP-error-rate spike
points to credential stuffing or a bad-deploy regression in the
login form, not an infrastructure outage.

Sources auth records by `event_type=auth` rather than by sourcetype
because the OTel collector OTTL transform that should carve out
`nwpay:auth` from the audit-tail stream relies on body regex
matching that does not always fire reliably; filtering on the
JSON-extracted `event_type` field is robust to that and works
whether the records land under `nwpay:auth` or the default
`nwpay:payment_audit` sourcetype.
base_search:
index=nwpay_audit event_type=auth
| bin _time span=1m
| stats count(eval(outcome="failed"))         as failed,
        count(eval(outcome="rate_limited"))   as rate_limited,
        count                                 as total
        by _time
| eval failure_rate     = round(failed / total, 4),
       rate_limited_pct = round(rate_limited / total, 4)

title: GuardDuty findings (24h)
description:
Count of GuardDuty findings per minute by severity bucket. Source:
Tier 3 Firehose pipeline (terraform/aws_logs_to_hec.tf). Returns 0
when Tier 3 is disabled or the AWS account has no findings.
base_search:
index=aws_guardduty sourcetype="aws:guardduty"
| rename detail.severity as severity
| bin _time span=1m
| stats count(eval(severity >= 7.0)) as high,
        count(eval(severity >= 4.0 AND severity < 7.0)) as medium,
        count(eval(severity < 4.0)) as low,
        count                       as total
        by _time

title: CloudTrail console logins without MFA
description:
Counts management console logins where MFA was not used. A non-zero
value is an immediate compliance flag for the demo's "MFA enforced
on production access" claim.
base_search:
index=aws_cloudtrail sourcetype="aws:cloudtrail"
  eventName="ConsoleLogin"
| rename additionalEventData.MFAUsed as mfa_used
| bin _time span=5m
| stats count(eval(mfa_used="No"))  as logins_without_mfa,
        count                        as total_logins
        by _time

title: Business outcomes - volume, value, customers, success
description:
Headline business KPIs derived from the structured banking audit
log. Drives the L1 NatWest Card Payments value-counter strip on
the glass table -- the four numbers an executive expects on a
single screen: payments per minute, value authorised in GBP,
customers impacted by failures in the last 5 minutes, and the
end-to-end success rate.

Source: index=nwpay_audit sourcetype=nwpay:payment_audit (Tier 2
audit pipeline, always on -- see helm/natwest-payments/values.yaml
api-gateway.auditEnabled=true). The api-gateway audit-tail sidecar
tails /var/log/audit/audit.jsonl emitted by app/audit.py and prints
each line to stdout; the splunk-otel agent's `transform/audit_routing`
processor (collector/values.yaml) routes records from any container
named `audit-tail` to `index=nwpay_audit sourcetype=nwpay:payment_audit`,
with `nwpay:auth` carved out for SPA auth-beacon events
(`event_type=auth`). Reads the same `decision`, `currency`,
`amount_minor_units` and `customer_id_hash` fields already validated
by app/audit.py emit_payment_audit() so the schema is stable.

`customers_impacted` is computed over a 5-minute window inside the
base search rather than relying on KPI aggregation, because
distinct-count of customer_id_hash collapses when ITSI rolls
multiple 1-minute buckets up with sum/avg.

Note: the demo gateway emits `decision="review"` (not `accepted`)
whenever a payment hits any downstream error, so success_rate_pct
counts both `accepted` and `review` as successful (the payment
cleared the gateway; review is just a flag for back-office, not
a customer-visible failure).
base_search:
index=nwpay_audit sourcetype="nwpay:payment_audit" event_type=payment_audit
| bin _time span=1m
| stats count(eval(decision IN ("accepted","review")))                                    as accepted,
        count                                                                              as total,
        sum(eval(if(decision IN ("accepted","review") AND currency="GBP", amount_minor_units, 0))) as gbp_minor_units,
        values(eval(if(decision IN ("rejected","throttled","error"), customer_id_hash, null()))) as failed_customers
        by _time
| eval payments_per_minute = total,
       value_authorised_gbp = round(gbp_minor_units / 100, 0),
       success_rate_pct     = round((accepted * 100) / total, 2),
       customers_impacted   = mvcount(failed_customers)
| eval customers_impacted   = coalesce(customers_impacted, 0)
| fields _time, payments_per_minute, value_authorised_gbp, customers_impacted, success_rate_pct
identifying_name: business outcomes - volume, value, customers, success

title: TE synthetic POST /api/process success rate
description:
ThousandEyes HTTP-server POST test (TE-05) - asserts the api-gateway
accepts a synthetic FPS payment write end-to-end. Success rate is
derived from http.server.request.availability (0-100 %) which TE
sets to 100 only when the response matches the configured status
code AND content regex (the JSON status: "accepted" / "partial"
check on TE-05). Closes the previous gap where TE-05 was created
but never had an ITSI KPI.
base_search:
index=thousandeyes sourcetype="cisco:thousandeyes:path-vis"
| rename "metric_name:http.server.request.availability" AS http_avail
| rename "thousandeyes.test.name"                       AS test_name
| rename "thousandeyes.test.id"                         AS test_id
| where test_name="LON NatWest Payments - POST /api/process" AND isnotnull(http_avail)
| bin _time span=1m
| stats avg(http_avail) AS availability_pct
        by _time, test_name, test_id
| eval success_rate = round(availability_pct / 100, 4)
| rename test_name AS te_test_name

title: TE synthetic POST /api/process p95 latency
description:
ThousandEyes HTTP-server POST test (TE-05) - p95 wall-clock time
from request send to last byte received. http.client.request.duration
is delivered in OTel seconds; converted to milliseconds.
base_search:
index=thousandeyes sourcetype="cisco:thousandeyes:path-vis"
| rename "metric_name:http.client.request.duration" AS http_dur_s
| rename "thousandeyes.test.name"                   AS test_name
| rename "thousandeyes.test.id"                     AS test_id
| where test_name="LON NatWest Payments - POST /api/process" AND isnotnull(http_dur_s)
| eval response_time_ms = http_dur_s * 1000
| bin _time span=1m
| stats perc95(response_time_ms) AS p95_ms
        by _time, test_name, test_id
| rename test_name AS te_test_name

title: TE geographic reachability (EMEA / NA / APAC)
description:
ThousandEyes HTTP-server test (TE-01) split by cloud-agent location
and bucketed into EMEA / NA / APAC regions. Tells the operator
which geography is degraded ("the bank is unreachable from APAC
right now") rather than just a single global average. The default
agent allocation in scripts/08-configure-thousandeyes.sh selects
London / Frankfurt / Amsterdam (EMEA), New York (NA) and
Singapore (APAC), so the regex below covers those plus a wider
set of common TE cloud-agent location names so adding more agents
doesn't silently drop into the OTHER bucket.
base_search:
index=thousandeyes sourcetype="cisco:thousandeyes:path-vis"
| rename "metric_name:http.server.request.availability" AS http_avail
| rename "thousandeyes.test.name"                       AS test_name
| rename "thousandeyes.source.agent.location"           AS agent_loc
| where test_name="LON NatWest Payments - SPA login page-load" AND isnotnull(http_avail)
| eval region = case(
      match(agent_loc, "(?i)(London|Frankfurt|Amsterdam|Paris|Dublin|Madrid|Milan|Stockholm|Berlin|Manchester|Zurich|Vienna|Brussels|Warsaw|Copenhagen|Helsinki|Lisbon|Oslo|Rome|Athens|Prague)"), "EMEA",
      match(agent_loc, "(?i)(New York|San Francisco|Chicago|Dallas|Los Angeles|Seattle|Atlanta|Toronto|Vancouver|Montreal|Miami|Washington|Boston|Denver|Phoenix|Houston|Mexico)"),                "NA",
      match(agent_loc, "(?i)(Singapore|Tokyo|Hong Kong|Sydney|Mumbai|Seoul|Bangkok|Jakarta|Beijing|Shanghai|Manila|Taipei|Melbourne|Auckland|Kuala Lumpur|Delhi|Bangalore|Chennai|Osaka)"), "APAC",
      true(), "OTHER")
| bin _time span=1m
| stats avg(http_avail) AS avail_pct by _time, region
| eval emea_pct = case(region="EMEA", avail_pct),
       na_pct   = case(region="NA",   avail_pct),
       apac_pct = case(region="APAC", avail_pct)
| stats max(emea_pct) AS emea_pct,
        max(na_pct)   AS na_pct,
        max(apac_pct) AS apac_pct
        by _time
| eval te_test_name = "LON NatWest Payments - SPA login page-load"

title: TE composite Digital Experience Index (0-100)
description:
Single 0-100 score blending the five user-facing ThousandEyes tests
with the same weighting an exec dashboard tile would use:
  0.30 * SPA availability (TE-01)
  0.30 * API gateway availability (TE-02)
  0.20 * end-to-end journey success (TE-04, scaled to 0-100)
  0.10 * page-load Apdex (TE-03; 1.0 if <=3s, 0.5 if <=8s, else 0)
  0.10 * DNS availability (TE-06)
Missing inputs default to 100 (treat as healthy) so a sparse 15min
cadence test (TE-04) doesn't drag the index down between probes.
multisearch with a per-leg src tag avoids cross-test cardinality
blow-up that a join would create.
base_search:
| multisearch
    [ search index=thousandeyes sourcetype="cisco:thousandeyes:path-vis"
        "thousandeyes.test.name"="LON NatWest Payments - SPA login page"
      | rename "metric_name:http.server.request.availability" AS spa_avail
      | where isnotnull(spa_avail)
      | eval src="spa", val=spa_avail ]
    [ search index=thousandeyes sourcetype="cisco:thousandeyes:path-vis"
        "thousandeyes.test.name"="LON NatWest Payments - API gateway recent"
      | rename "metric_name:http.server.request.availability" AS api_avail
      | where isnotnull(api_avail)
      | eval src="api", val=api_avail ]
    [ search index=thousandeyes sourcetype="cisco:thousandeyes:path-vis"
        "thousandeyes.test.name"="LON NatWest Payments - end-to-end payment journey"
      | rename "metric_name:web.transaction.completion" AS journey_succ
      | where isnotnull(journey_succ)
      | eval src="journey", val=journey_succ*100 ]
    [ search index=thousandeyes sourcetype="cisco:thousandeyes:path-vis"
        "thousandeyes.test.name"="LON NatWest Payments - SPA login page-load"
      | rename "metric_name:web.page_load.duration" AS pl_s
      | where isnotnull(pl_s)
      | eval pl_ms = pl_s * 1000,
             pl_apdex = case(pl_ms <= 3000, 1.0, pl_ms <= 8000, 0.5, true(), 0.0),
             src = "pageload", val = pl_apdex * 100 ]
    [ search index=thousandeyes sourcetype="cisco:thousandeyes:path-vis"
        "thousandeyes.test.name"="LON NatWest Payments - DNS resolution of demo hostname"
      | rename "metric_name:dns.lookup.availability" AS dns_avail
      | where isnotnull(dns_avail)
      | eval src="dns", val=dns_avail ]
| bin _time span=1m
| stats avg(eval(if(src="spa",      val, null()))) AS spa_score,
        avg(eval(if(src="api",      val, null()))) AS api_score,
        avg(eval(if(src="journey",  val, null()))) AS journey_score,
        avg(eval(if(src="pageload", val, null()))) AS pageload_score,
        avg(eval(if(src="dns",      val, null()))) AS dns_score
        by _time
| eval spa_score      = coalesce(spa_score, 100),
       api_score      = coalesce(api_score, 100),
       journey_score  = coalesce(journey_score, 100),
       pageload_score = coalesce(pageload_score, 100),
       dns_score      = coalesce(dns_score, 100)
| eval dx_index = round(0.30 * spa_score
                      + 0.30 * api_score
                      + 0.20 * journey_score
                      + 0.10 * pageload_score
                      + 0.10 * dns_score, 1)

title: TE journey SLO error-budget burn rate (99.9%)
description:
Multi-window error-budget burn rate for the TE-04 journey against
a 99.9% monthly success SLO. Per Google SRE multi-window fast-burn:
  burn = (1 - success_rate_window) / (1 - SLO)
Critical when 1h burn > 14.4 (ie. 2% of monthly budget burned in
the last hour). Window is computed via streamstats over per-minute
rows; TE-04 cadence is 15 min so 1h yields ~4 samples and 6h
yields ~24, which is enough signal-to-noise for the demo.
base_search:
index=thousandeyes sourcetype="cisco:thousandeyes:path-vis"
    "thousandeyes.test.name"="LON NatWest Payments - SPA login page-load"
| rename "metric_name:http.server.request.availability" AS avail_pct
| where isnotnull(avail_pct)
| bin _time span=1m
| stats avg(avail_pct) AS avail_pct by _time
| eval success_rate = avail_pct / 100.0
| streamstats current=t window=60  avg(success_rate) AS sr_1h
| streamstats current=t window=360 avg(success_rate) AS sr_6h
| eval burn_1h = round((1 - coalesce(sr_1h, 1.0)) / 0.001, 2),
       burn_6h = round((1 - coalesce(sr_6h, 1.0)) / 0.001, 2),
       te_test_name = "LON NatWest Payments - SPA login page-load"
identifying_name: te journey slo error-budget burn rate (99.9%)

title: TE revenue / customers at risk (synthetic-driven)
description:
Cross-references the TE-04 success rate with the live banking-audit
baseline to estimate, per minute:
  blocked_payments_per_min  = baseline_payments_per_min  * (1 - synthetic_success)
  gbp_at_risk_per_min       = baseline_gbp_per_min       * (1 - synthetic_success)
  customers_blocked_per_min = baseline_customers_per_min * (1 - synthetic_success)
Baseline figures are an avg over the last hour of audit events
(index=nwpay_audit sourcetype="nwpay:payment_audit", same source
kbs_business_outcomes uses) so this stays steady even when TE-04's
15-minute cadence makes synthetic data sparse. The result is
"what your customers are losing right now if the synthetic check
is right" - the most CFO-friendly KPI in the tree.
base_search:
| multisearch
    [ search index=thousandeyes sourcetype="cisco:thousandeyes:path-vis"
        "thousandeyes.test.name"="LON NatWest Payments - end-to-end payment journey"
      | rename "metric_name:web.transaction.completion" AS tx_completion
      | where isnotnull(tx_completion)
      | eval src="te", te_success_rate = tx_completion ]
    [ search index=nwpay_audit sourcetype="nwpay:payment_audit"
      | eval src="audit",
             audit_payment = 1,
             audit_gbp     = if(currency="GBP", amount_minor_units / 100.0, 0),
             audit_cust    = customer_id_hash ]
| bin _time span=1m
| stats avg(eval(if(src="te",    te_success_rate, null()))) AS te_success_rate,
        sum(eval(if(src="audit", audit_payment,   null()))) AS pmin,
        sum(eval(if(src="audit", audit_gbp,       null()))) AS gbpmin,
        dc(audit_cust)                                       AS cmin
        by _time
| streamstats current=t window=60 avg(pmin) AS baseline_pmin,
                                  avg(gbpmin) AS baseline_gbpmin,
                                  avg(cmin) AS baseline_cmin
| eval failure_factor = 1 - coalesce(te_success_rate, 1.0),
       blocked_payments_per_min  = round(coalesce(baseline_pmin, 0)   * failure_factor, 1),
       gbp_at_risk_per_min       = round(coalesce(baseline_gbpmin, 0) * failure_factor, 0),
       customers_blocked_per_min = round(coalesce(baseline_cmin, 0)   * failure_factor, 0),
       te_test_name = "LON NatWest Payments - end-to-end payment journey"
| fields _time, blocked_payments_per_min, gbp_at_risk_per_min, customers_blocked_per_min, te_test_name

title: TE DNS-outage blocked customers (synthetic-driven)
description:
DNS-layer outage blast radius. dns_avail/100 from TE-06 multiplied
against the audit-log baseline to give "customers / min unable to
reach the bank because DNS is broken". Different signal from
kbs_te_revenue_at_risk because DNS failures don't show up in
app-level error rates - the resolver simply doesn't return an
address, the client never connects, and APM stays green.

        "thousandeyes.test.name"="LON NatWest Payments - DNS resolution of demo hostname"
      | rename "metric_name:dns.lookup.availability" AS dns_avail
      | where isnotnull(dns_avail)

      | eval src="audit", audit_payment = 1 ]
| bin _time span=1m
| stats avg(eval(if(src="dns",   dns_ratio,     null()))) AS dns_ratio,
        sum(eval(if(src="audit", audit_payment, null()))) AS pmin
        by _time
| streamstats current=t window=60 avg(pmin) AS baseline_pmin

title: TE synthetic outage minutes (rolling 1h)
description:
Counts minutes in the last 60 where either the SPA HTTP probe
(TE-01) reported avail < 99% OR the end-to-end journey (TE-04)
reported success < 50%. Rolling sum gives a stable "minutes of

| where isnotnull(spa_avail)
| bin _time span=1m

title: TE end-to-end journey Apdex (T 20s / F 60s)
description:
Apdex score for the TE-04 web-transaction journey. Per Apdex:
  Apdex = (satisfied + 0.5 * tolerating) / total
where satisfied = transactions <= T, tolerating = T < t <= F. T
and F here are 20s / 60s, matching the TE test transactionTimeLimit
(60s) and the in-flight UX target. Drives the "Journey Apdex" KPI
on the synthetic outcomes service - more diagnostic than a binary
success rate because slow journeys still count as 0.5. Title
uses '/' instead of '=' because the ITSI REST API rejects '=' in
kpi_base_search titles.
base_search:
index=thousandeyes sourcetype="cisco:thousandeyes:path-vis"
    "thousandeyes.test.name"="LON NatWest Payments - POST /api/process*"
| rename "thousandeyes.test.name" AS test_name
| rename "metric_name:http.client.request.duration" AS dur_s
| where isnotnull(dur_s)
| eval tx_ms = dur_s * 1000
| bin _time span=1m
| stats count(eval(tx_ms <= 20000))                   AS satisfied,
        count(eval(tx_ms > 20000 AND tx_ms <= 60000)) AS tolerating,
        count                                         AS total
        by _time
| where total > 0
| eval apdex = round((satisfied + 0.5 * tolerating) / total, 3)
| eval te_test_name = "LON NatWest Payments - POST /api/process (all locations)"

title: Payments by customer location (p95 latency, RPS, error rate)
description:
Per-minute APM aggregates split by customer.location (the city the
payment originated from). Drives the L2 "Payments by Location"
service so a regional latency story (e.g. Madrid client-side RTT
degradation) shows up as one bad city rather than a global p95
lift.

Source is the api-gateway server span - that's where the SDK has
finished extracting the customer.location attribute from the
JSON body, so every row has a populated city. Spans without a
location (e.g. internal health checks) are dropped by the
`customer_location!=""` filter so they don't poison the bucket
with empty-string rows.

The same KBS also surfaces the roaming-payment p95 (filter
`payment.roaming=true`) so the fraud-detection story has a
single, stable KPI it can pivot on.
base_search:
index=otel_traces sourcetype="otel:traces" service.name=api-gateway
  (kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER" OR span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER")
| rename "attributes.customer.location" as customer_location
| rename "attributes.customer.country"  as customer_country
| rename "attributes.customer.region"   as customer_region
| rename "attributes.payment.roaming"   as payment_roaming
| rename "status.code"                  as status_code
| where isnotnull(customer_location) AND customer_location!=""
| eval duration_ns = coalesce(duration_ns, end_time - start_time)
| bin _time span=1m
| stats perc95(duration_ns) as p95_ns,
        perc99(duration_ns) as p99_ns,
        count               as rpm,
        count(eval(status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR" OR 'error'="true")) as errors
        by _time, customer_location, customer_country, customer_region, payment_roaming
| eval p95_ms     = round(p95_ns / 1000000, 0),
       p99_ms     = round(p99_ns / 1000000, 0),
       rps        = round(rpm / 60.0, 2),
       error_rate = round(errors / rpm, 4)
identifying_name: payments by customer location (p95 latency, rps, error rate)

description:

Drives the "Postgres long-running txns" KPI on the

title: Kubernetes workload health (natwest namespace - pods, deployments, restarts)
description:
Live snapshot of every pod / container / deployment in the `natwest`
Kubernetes namespace, fed by the splunk-otel-collector cluster
receiver. Powers the L4 nwpay_l4_kubernetes service.

Fields emitted per 1-minute bucket:
  * running_pods             count(k8s.pod.phase=2) in natwest
  * pending_pods             count(k8s.pod.phase=1)
  * failed_pods              count(k8s.pod.phase=4)
  * containers_ready         count(k8s.container.ready=1)
  * deployment_avail_ratio   sum(available) / sum(desired)
  * container_restarts_total cumulative restart counter (sum
                              across all natwest containers)
  * container_restarts_5m    streamstats range() of the above over
                              a 6-bucket window

Implementation note: we use `| union [...] [...]` rather than
`| multisearch [...] [...]`. This Splunk build's multisearch
command silently drops mstats-generating subsearches (returns an
empty result set with no error) -- union accepts them cleanly.
Verified live with mcatalog 2026-06-17.
base_search:
| union
    [ mstats latest(_value) AS phase
        WHERE index=itsi_im_metrics metric_name=k8s.pod.phase
              "k8s.namespace.name"=natwest
        BY "k8s.pod.name" span=1m
      | eval src="phase" ]
    [ mstats latest(_value) AS ready
        WHERE index=itsi_im_metrics metric_name=k8s.container.ready
              "k8s.namespace.name"=natwest
        BY "k8s.container.name" "k8s.pod.name" span=1m
      | eval src="ready" ]
    [ mstats latest(_value) AS rcount
        WHERE index=itsi_im_metrics metric_name=k8s.container.restarts
              "k8s.namespace.name"=natwest
        BY "k8s.container.name" "k8s.pod.name" span=1m
      | eval src="restarts" ]
    [ mstats latest(_value) AS d_avail
        WHERE index=itsi_im_metrics metric_name=k8s.deployment.available
              "k8s.namespace.name"=natwest
        BY "k8s.deployment.name" span=1m
      | eval src="dep_avail" ]
    [ mstats latest(_value) AS d_desired
        WHERE index=itsi_im_metrics metric_name=k8s.deployment.desired
              "k8s.namespace.name"=natwest
        BY "k8s.deployment.name" span=1m
      | eval src="dep_desired" ]
| bin _time span=1m
| stats sum(eval(if(src="phase"       AND phase=2,  1, 0))) AS running_pods,
        sum(eval(if(src="phase"       AND phase=1,  1, 0))) AS pending_pods,
        sum(eval(if(src="phase"       AND phase=4,  1, 0))) AS failed_pods,
        sum(eval(if(src="ready"       AND ready=1,  1, 0))) AS containers_ready,
        sum(eval(if(src="dep_avail",   d_avail,   null()))) AS deployments_available,
        sum(eval(if(src="dep_desired", d_desired, null()))) AS deployments_desired,
        sum(eval(if(src="restarts",    rcount,    null()))) AS container_restarts_total
        BY _time
| eval deployment_avail_ratio = if(deployments_desired>0, round(deployments_available / deployments_desired, 4), 1)
| timechart span=1m fixedrange=t partial=f
        max(running_pods)              AS running_pods,
        max(pending_pods)              AS pending_pods,
        max(failed_pods)               AS failed_pods,
        max(containers_ready)          AS containers_ready,
        max(deployment_avail_ratio)    AS deployment_avail_ratio,
        max(container_restarts_total)  AS container_restarts_total
| fillnull value=0 running_pods pending_pods failed_pods containers_ready container_restarts_total
| fillnull value=1 deployment_avail_ratio
| streamstats current=t window=6 range(container_restarts_total) AS container_restarts_5m
| eval container_restarts_5m = coalesce(container_restarts_5m, 0)
identifying_name: kubernetes workload health (natwest namespace - pods, deployments, restarts)

title: Splunk OTel Collector pipeline health (agent + cluster receiver + self-metrics)
description:
Live health of the splunk-otel-collector workload and its
telemetry pipeline. Powers the L4 nwpay_l4_otel_collector service.

Fields emitted per 1-minute bucket:
  * agent_ready_ratio          DaemonSet ready / desired
  * cluster_receiver_avail     cluster-receiver Deployment available replicas
  * queue_size                 max exporter queue depth across pods
  * send_failed_spans_5m       streamstats range over 6-bucket window
  * recv_refused_spans_5m      streamstats range over 6-bucket window
  * recv_failed_spans_5m       streamstats range over 6-bucket window
  * sent_spans_per_sec         informational throughput context
  * collector_uptime_min       min uptime across collector pods --
                                drops to 0 on restart, so a sudden
                                low value flags a restart event

Same implementation note as kbs_k8s_natwest_workloads above: we
use `| union [...] [...]` rather than `| multisearch [...] [...]`
because this Splunk build's multisearch silently drops
mstats-generating subsearches.

Note on `span=1m` vs `BY span=1m`: when an mstats subsearch has no
dimension to group on (e.g. otelcol_exporter_queue_size aggregated
globally), the syntax is `... span=1m` (no BY) -- `BY span=1m`
raises "Missing field list after 'BY' keyword". Subsearches that
DO have a dimension (none in this base search, but several in
kbs_k8s_natwest_workloads) use `BY <field> span=1m`.
base_search:
| union
    [ mstats latest(_value) AS daemon_ready
        WHERE index=itsi_im_metrics metric_name=k8s.daemonset.ready_nodes
              "k8s.daemonset.name"="splunk-otel-collector-agent"
        span=1m
      | eval src="daemon_ready" ]
    [ mstats latest(_value) AS daemon_desired
        WHERE index=itsi_im_metrics metric_name=k8s.daemonset.desired_scheduled_nodes
              "k8s.daemonset.name"="splunk-otel-collector-agent"
        span=1m
      | eval src="daemon_desired" ]
    [ mstats latest(_value) AS cr_avail
        WHERE index=itsi_im_metrics metric_name=k8s.deployment.available
              "k8s.deployment.name"="splunk-otel-collector-cluster-receiver"
        span=1m
      | eval src="cluster_receiver" ]
    [ mstats max(_value) AS queue
        WHERE index=itsi_im_metrics metric_name=otelcol_exporter_queue_size
        span=1m
      | eval src="queue" ]
    [ mstats sum(_value) AS sf_spans
        WHERE index=itsi_im_metrics metric_name=otelcol_exporter_send_failed_spans
        span=1m
      | eval src="sf_spans" ]
    [ mstats sum(_value) AS rr_spans
        WHERE index=itsi_im_metrics metric_name=otelcol_receiver_refused_spans
        span=1m
      | eval src="rr_spans" ]
    [ mstats sum(_value) AS rf_spans
        WHERE index=itsi_im_metrics metric_name=otelcol_receiver_failed_spans
        span=1m
      | eval src="rf_spans" ]
    [ mstats sum(_value) AS s_spans
        WHERE index=itsi_im_metrics metric_name=otelcol_exporter_sent_spans
        span=1m
      | eval src="s_spans" ]
    [ mstats min(_value) AS uptime
        WHERE index=itsi_im_metrics metric_name=otelcol_process_uptime
        span=1m
      | eval src="uptime" ]
| bin _time span=1m
| stats sum(eval(if(src="daemon_ready",     daemon_ready,   null()))) AS daemon_ready,
        sum(eval(if(src="daemon_desired",   daemon_desired, null()))) AS daemon_desired,
        max(eval(if(src="cluster_receiver", cr_avail,       null()))) AS cluster_receiver_avail,
        max(eval(if(src="queue",            queue,          null()))) AS queue_size,
        sum(eval(if(src="sf_spans",         sf_spans,       null()))) AS send_failed_spans_total,
        sum(eval(if(src="rr_spans",         rr_spans,       null()))) AS recv_refused_spans_total,
        sum(eval(if(src="rf_spans",         rf_spans,       null()))) AS recv_failed_spans_total,
        sum(eval(if(src="s_spans",          s_spans,        null()))) AS sent_spans_total,
        min(eval(if(src="uptime",           uptime,         null()))) AS collector_uptime_seconds
        BY _time
| eval agent_ready_ratio = if(daemon_desired>0, round(daemon_ready / daemon_desired, 4), 1)
| timechart span=1m fixedrange=t partial=f
        max(agent_ready_ratio)         AS agent_ready_ratio,
        max(cluster_receiver_avail)    AS cluster_receiver_avail,
        max(queue_size)                AS queue_size,
        max(send_failed_spans_total)   AS send_failed_spans_total,
        max(recv_refused_spans_total)  AS recv_refused_spans_total,
        max(recv_failed_spans_total)   AS recv_failed_spans_total,
        max(sent_spans_total)          AS sent_spans_total,
        min(collector_uptime_seconds)  AS collector_uptime_seconds
| fillnull value=1 agent_ready_ratio cluster_receiver_avail
| fillnull value=0 queue_size send_failed_spans_total recv_refused_spans_total recv_failed_spans_total sent_spans_total
| fillnull value=86400 collector_uptime_seconds
| streamstats current=t window=6
        range(send_failed_spans_total)  AS send_failed_spans_5m,
        range(recv_refused_spans_total) AS recv_refused_spans_5m,
        range(recv_failed_spans_total)  AS recv_failed_spans_5m,
        range(sent_spans_total)         AS sent_spans_5m_total
| eval send_failed_spans_5m  = coalesce(send_failed_spans_5m, 0),
       recv_refused_spans_5m = coalesce(recv_refused_spans_5m, 0),
       recv_failed_spans_5m  = coalesce(recv_failed_spans_5m, 0),
       sent_spans_per_sec    = round(coalesce(sent_spans_5m_total, 0) / 300, 0),
       collector_uptime_min  = round(coalesce(collector_uptime_seconds, 86400) / 60, 0)
identifying_name: splunk otel collector pipeline health (agent + cluster receiver + self-metrics)

title: splunk-otel-collector - per-pod breakdown
description:
Per-pod liveness and throughput for the splunk-otel-collector
workload (agent DaemonSet pods + cluster-receiver pod). Powers
the entity-aware KPI on nwpay_l4_otel_collector.

Fields emitted per 1-minute bucket per pod:
  * uptime_min        otelcol_process_uptime / 60 (min)
  * queue_size        max exporter queue depth this minute
  * sent_per_sec      delta(otelcol_exporter_sent_spans) / 300
base_search:
| union
    [ mstats latest(_value) AS uptime
        WHERE index=itsi_im_metrics metric_name=otelcol_process_uptime
        BY "k8s.pod.name" span=1m
      | rename "k8s.pod.name" AS k8s_pod_name
      | eval src="uptime" ]
    [ mstats max(_value) AS queue
        WHERE index=itsi_im_metrics metric_name=otelcol_exporter_queue_size
        BY "k8s.pod.name" span=1m
      | rename "k8s.pod.name" AS k8s_pod_name
      | eval src="queue" ]
    [ mstats latest(_value) AS sent_total
        WHERE index=itsi_im_metrics metric_name=otelcol_exporter_sent_spans
        BY "k8s.pod.name" span=1m
      | rename "k8s.pod.name" AS k8s_pod_name
      | eval src="sent" ]
| bin _time span=1m
| stats max(eval(if(src="uptime", uptime,    null()))) AS uptime_seconds,
        max(eval(if(src="queue",  queue,     null()))) AS queue_size,
        max(eval(if(src="sent",   sent_total,null()))) AS sent_total
        BY _time, k8s_pod_name
| where isnotnull(k8s_pod_name)
| streamstats current=t window=6 range(sent_total) AS sent_5m by k8s_pod_name
| eval uptime_min   = round(uptime_seconds / 60, 0),
       sent_per_sec = round(coalesce(sent_5m, 0) / 300, 1)
| fillnull value=0 queue_size sent_per_sec
| fillnull value=10000 uptime_min

| eval rt_ms = round('metric_name:http.client.request.duration'*1000, 1)
| where isnotnull(rt_ms)
| table _time rt_ms

title: Payments p95 latency (london)
base_search:
index=otel_traces sourcetype="otel:traces" service.name=api-gateway
  (kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER" OR span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER")
| rename "attributes.customer.location" as customer_location
| where customer_location="london"
| eval duration_ns = coalesce(duration_ns, end_time - start_time)
| bin _time span=1m
| stats perc95(duration_ns) as p95_ns by _time
| eval p95_ms = round(p95_ns / 1000000, 0)
| fields _time p95_ms
